To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the exciton binding energy is a monotonically decreasing function of the applied electric field, of the cylinder radius and of its height.
the binding energy of excitons confined in a cylindrical quantum dot is a decreasing function both of the quantum dot size and the electric field intensity.
the exciton binding energy and the nonlinear optical response of a cylindrical quantum dot can be modified by the application of an external electric field along the cylinder growth direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the electric field on exciton properties in cylindrical quantum dots.

the influence of an electric field and of the quantum dots geometry on the exciton binding energy, the exciton nonlinear optical properties and their potential use in the development of quantum dot-based optoelectronic devices.
the influence on exciton binding energy and on the nonlinear optical absorption and rectification properties of cylindrical quantum dots of the application of external electric fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in general, the electric field effects are more important than the quantum confinement ones, and the nonlinear optical properties are more sensible to the electric field effects than to the quantum confinement.

the exciton properties in the quantum dots are very sensitive to the applied electric field and that the electric field effects on the optical properties can be tuned through the variation of the quantum dot dimensions and the aluminum content in the barrier regions.
the exciton binding energy decreases as the electric field strength is increased.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exciton binding energy and nonlinear optical absorption and rectification resonant peak energies are strongly affected by the quantum dot geometry and the applied electric field.
the electric field effects in cylindrical quantum dots could be an important tool to control the exciton related optical properties.
the electric field effects on the excitons are more important in quantum dots with smaller height and larger radius.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to control the exciton properties in quantum dots by means of an external electric field.
, given an appropriate quantum dot size, the electric field effects can be exploited to enhance the exciton related optical nonlinearities.
the exciton related resonant peaks are very sensitive to the electric field strength, and the electric field effects can be used to tune the optical nonlinear properties of these nanostructures.
